question.text: In an experiment to determine the velocity of sound in air at room temperature using a resonance tube, the first resonance is observed when the air column has a length of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> for a tuning fork of frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>400</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> is used. The velocity of the sound at room temperature is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>336</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The third resonance is observed when the air column has a length of _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>

solution.text:
Wavelength of wave ⇒λ=vf=336400=84 cm

At first resonance

λ4=l+e⇒844=20+e, where, e is end correction.

⇒e=1
So third resonance length

5λ4=l2+e

521=l2+1

l2=104 cm
